about: 10CL016 embedded multipliers (offline; xdev macm:WA:WB:SA:SB:CKIN:CKOUT, cyclone10lp_mac_mult pinned at DSPMULT_X18_Y<y>_N0 with its mac_out at DSPOUT_X18_Y<y>_N2; the multiplier column is X18). Sign bits: signa at (frame 940, ROW[y].low - 29, ROW[y].plane), signb at ROW[y].low - 31, set = signed, with the usual byte wrap (byte < 1). Fitted at Y10, Y12, Y20 and predicted blind at 8 more rows (8/8). Input/output registers and 9-bit mode change 1300-2000 bits including DSP-column routing; not separated.

mode_candidates.about: From macm: builds at X18Y10 and X18Y20 with the 36-bit input shift register pinned (frame offset from 940, byte offset from ROW[y].low, plane offset, value when the mode is on); kept only if identical at both sites. Offline, not tested on silicon; the rest of each diff is routing (clocks to the block, unused input lines, the output parity tree).
mode_candidates.silicon: 2026-11-23 (dspram_test.py, X18Y10): 9x9 bit confirmed: the product splits into two 9x9 products (80/80 clocks; parity can't tell which half goes where). Register bits NOT confirmed: with the input/output-register candidates (+ the 4 clock bits) D5 stayed at 0 in all three files (mismatches = the predicted 1s), i.e. the registers are in the path but never clock or sit cleared. Probably their clock/ena/aclr inputs need routing bits that Quartus's registered builds add (70-127 more DSP-column bits); left for the routing work.
